summary: A report by Jon Postel on decisions at the protocol workshop of the October 1971 Network Working Group meeting. It covers IMP-Host, Host-Host, initial connection and process-process protocols, including rules about spontaneous commands in the host-host protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 295 reports on protocol discussions held with the October 1971 Network Working Group meeting. It records decisions and open questions about host communication, connection setup and Telnet.

subtitle: Decisions and open questions from the October 1971 protocol workshop.

tldr.problem: Early protocol documents needed clarification after implementation raised questions about command use, connection handling and Telnet behavior.
tldr.mechanism: The workshop reviewed IMP-Host, Host-Host, Initial Connection and Telnet protocols and recorded decisions, restrictions and issues for further work.
tldr.outcome: The report documents workshop conclusions and follow-up topics; the Data and File Transfer Committee was to report separately.

sections.title: Workshop Scope
sections.content:
The protocol workshop was held with the Network Working Group meeting in Cambridge from October 10-14, 1971. It addressed IMP-Host, Host-Host, Initial Connection and Process-Process protocols.

The report records discussions and recommendations, including decisions to reject one proposed IMP-Host status-report mechanism and to clarify command behavior in other protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: The workshop reviewed several layers of network communication. This report summarizes decisions and questions that needed more work.

sections.title: Host-Host and ICP Decisions
sections.content:
The report says the GVB-RET mechanism would be retained, while spontaneous RET commands were prohibited. ECO-ERP commands should be supported, but a second ECO should wait until the first receives an answer. Spontaneous ERP and RRP commands were also prohibited.

The workshop discussed unmatched CLS commands and asked that NCP documentation clarify whether STR and RTS commands are queued. It found the ICP satisfactory, while stressing that the logger's socket number must match the sockets used in STR and RTS commands.
sections.plainLanguage: The workshop set limits on when certain commands could be sent and called for clearer documentation. It also identified socket-number matching as important during connection setup.

sections.title: Telnet Follow-Up
sections.content:
The Telnet committee was reactivated to clarify terms such as half duplex, full duplex, character mode, line mode, ASCII and echoing. It was also asked to clarify end-of-line behavior, Hide-your-input mode, Break and Synch, and the Network Virtual Terminal.

The workshop agreed that servers could choose whether disconnection implied logout and whether logout implied disconnection. It also defined Synch as examining the data stream to a data mark and giving break-type characters their normal effect.
sections.plainLanguage: The Telnet committee would clarify terms and behaviors that could be interpreted in different ways. The workshop also recorded server choices for logout and disconnection.
